clause: Fundamental decomposition and fixed sector projections
evidence_or_owed: The grading gives the two fixed sector projections and the Krein-orthogonal positive and negative summands. The positive Hilbert product determines norms and operator domains.

clause: Oddness and unbounded domains
evidence_or_owed: On a grading-invariant domain the sector projections split the domain. Oddness is equivalent to the vanishing of both diagonal blocks there.

clause: Odd-adjoint signs for the polar operators
evidence_or_owed: Section 3 gives the opposite Hilbert and Krein adjoint types of the bounded phase operators and the rotation generator.

clause: Both equivalences for arbitrary densely defined closed odd X
evidence_or_owed: The Hilbert adjoint of an odd operator is odd with a grading-invariant domain. Conjugation by the grading therefore gives the negative Hilbert adjoint, including its domain. This gives both equivalences.

clause: Sign distinction for structural phase operators
evidence_or_owed: The text states the Hilbert and Krein adjoint types of these operators on the active carrier.

clause: General odd-branch interpretation
evidence_or_owed: The general odd-adjoint equivalences apply to the two sums built from one closed channel. They exchange the Hilbert and Krein adjoint signs.

clause: Two-dimensional Krein-self-adjoint normal form
evidence_or_owed: For a two-by-two odd matrix, Krein self-adjointness fixes the lower coefficient as the negative conjugate of the upper coefficient. A diagonal phase preserving the grading makes the nonzero upper coefficient positive.

clause: Closed densely defined map between the two sectors and its Hilbert adjoint
evidence_or_owed: Sections 1 and 7 use A with its original domain and Hilbert adjoint throughout.

clause: Two oriented transitions and signs
evidence_or_owed: The full-sum formula gives the signed forward map as −d_A and the return map as d_A*. Their domains leave different sector coordinates unrestricted.

clause: Density, closedness, nilpotency and square domains of the differential and its adjoint
evidence_or_owed: The two triangular operators are dense and closed. Each maps its first-order domain into itself and vanishes on the summand containing its image, so its square has the same domain.

clause: Four named operators and Hilbert and Krein adjoints of the oriented pair
evidence_or_owed: The differential, its adjoint and the two signed orientations are defined on their full triangular domains. The Hilbert adjoints exchange the signed orientations with a minus sign and the Krein adjoints exchange them with a plus sign.

clause: Unique signed block representation and its converse
evidence_or_owed: The grading splits the domain into dense sector domains. The block adjoint identifies the two closed off-diagonal entries up to the required sign. The lower block recovers the channel uniquely, and the block construction gives the converse.

clause: Common first-order domain of the two odd combinations
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 places d_A+d_A* and d_A*−d_A on Dom A plus Dom A*.

clause: Hilbert and Krein adjoints, signed squares, and relation K=JD
evidence_or_owed: The two odd sums have opposite Hilbert and Krein adjoint signs and differ by left multiplication by the grading. Their squares are the positive and negative partner Laplacian on its product domain.

clause: Equality of the two moduli and both adjoint-products
evidence_or_owed: Both adjoint-products equal the positive partner Laplacian, so its positive square root is the common modulus.

clause: Equal carriers coupled by one self-adjoint operator
evidence_or_owed: For separate sector copies of one Hilbert space and a self-adjoint channel, the two branches are the indicated Pauli factors tensored with that channel. Its modulus is the absolute value of the self-adjoint channel.

clause: Domain-aware algebra of the two signed orientations
evidence_or_owed: The signed orientations have zero squares on their first-order domains. Their two ordered products have different composition domains. On their intersection the anticommutator is minus the Laplacian and the ordinary commutator is the grading times the Laplacian. The sum and difference give the two branches.

clause: Positivity and self-adjointness of both sector returns
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 states that both A*A and AA* are positive self-adjoint.

clause: Two single-sector closed-form identities
evidence_or_owed: The two closed sector forms have domains Dom A and Dom A* and values equal to the squared norms under the square roots of the respective positive return operators.

clause: Common two-sector energy on the first-order domain
evidence_or_owed: On the direct sum of the form domains, both branch norms squared equal the sum of the two sector forms and the norm squared of the Laplacian square root.

clause: Partner kernels and harmonic sum
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 identifies the kernel of the block-diagonal Laplacian with ker A plus ker A*, using orthogonal decompositions.

clause: Common zero modes of both odd branches for Fredholm A
evidence_or_owed: The Fredholm argument identifies both odd kernels with the harmonic kernel.

clause: Same odd-kernel identity for every closed dense A
evidence_or_owed: The two branches vanish on exactly the input and output sector kernels, which together form the kernel of the Laplacian for any closed densely defined channel.

clause: Shared zero modes and magnitude with opposite square signs
evidence_or_owed: The branches have a common kernel and a common positive modulus, while their squares have opposite signs on the second-order domain.

clause: Norms and vanishing of a reference image
evidence_or_owed: The signed image of a unit input reference has Hilbert norm squared equal to the squared norm of its channel image and the opposite Krein square. It vanishes precisely for a reference in the kernel.

clause: Forward annihilation and backward return for the signed reference image
evidence_or_owed: The forward map annihilates every such image on its first-order domain. A second step by the return map exists exactly on the input product domain and gives minus the input return there.

clause: The symmetry average is a separate object from the sector projections and a moving projection, with its own notation
evidence_or_owed: The section defines the Haar projection and distinguishes it from the grading, support and preparation projections after the compatibility proposition.

clause: Haar average and its invariant range
evidence_or_owed: The average is defined by its matrix elements, and one sentence identifies it with TAUM's vector integral. Boundedness, idempotence, self-adjointness, the invariant range and absorption of the representation on both sides are proved.

clause: Compatibility with the grading
evidence_or_owed: Part (a): when the representation commutes with the sector symmetry, the invariant projection commutes with it, is the direct sum of the invariant projections of the two sectors, and equals its adjoint for the indefinite form.

clause: Finite average and trivial cubic representation
draft_quote: For a finite group of rotations of a cube
evidence_or_owed: The normalized finite sum is part of the proposition. The sentence after its proof identifies the average over a group of cube rotations with the projection onto the vectors on which that group acts trivially.

clause: Distinguishing the four projections and the two symmetry groups
draft_quote: Its construction does not identify it with any of them.
evidence_or_owed: The invariant projection is separated from the sector projection, the support projections and a prepared or moving projection. In the pair model it equals the prepared projection at one setting, commutes with it at another and does neither in between. The difference between a finite and a continuous group is shown by the cube rotations on homogeneous quartic polynomials and by the cyclic subgroups of the orbital rotations, where the quarter turns stay a symmetry at every coupling and have the same invariant projection as the circle.

clause: Identity for the particular partner of the output ground, including fidelity one
evidence_or_owed: Section 4 removes the ground component, computes the conditional mean and separately gives zero excess at fidelity one.

clause: Arbitrary unit test state in Dom H
evidence_or_owed: Part (a) holds for every unit vector of the form domain, which contains Dom H, with the case of fidelity one stated separately and without reference to a preparation.

clause: Nonnegative conditional excitation scale for any eligible state
evidence_or_owed: For fidelity below one the scale Z is defined as the excitation energy of the normalized orthogonal component and shown nonnegative. The text gives it an operational meaning through the Lüders test of the chosen ray, says that it depends on the state and when it is constant, and bounds it by the gap and by the width of a bounded spectrum.

clause: Gap bound for the ground partner on the operator domain
evidence_or_owed: Section 4 gives 1−F ≤ ε/Δ from an upper bound ε on the mean excess energy and the gap on the reference complement.

clause: General inequality on the full quadratic-form domain
evidence_or_owed: The excitation energy is defined on the form domain by the square root, and part (b) proves the inequality for every unit vector there under the form gap. A state of the number operator with finite mean and infinite second moment shows that the form domain is strictly larger.

clause: Fubini–Study form of the arbitrary input-state energy-gap estimate
evidence_or_owed: The distance is defined with the modulus of the overlap, measured from the ray of the ground, and the bound is displayed in that form.

clause: The fidelity results apply to any self-adjoint realization whose ground and domain hypotheses hold, and use no cyclicity
draft_quote: No cyclicity is used.
evidence_or_owed: TAUM lines 1327 to 1349. The last paragraph names the three operators to which the proposition can be applied, says that the hypotheses must be checked in each case, that a reference vector with nonzero image need not be a ground of the return and a ground in the kernel has zero image, and that cyclicity is not used.

clause: Polar factor, initial and final spaces, and support projections
evidence_or_owed: Sections 1–2 specify A=u|A|, its zero action on ker A, the active supports, closure of ran A*, closure of ran A, and both projection products.

clause: Uniqueness with prescribed initial support; remaining polar identities
evidence_or_owed: The initial support and prescribed zero action on the kernel determine the polar partial isometry uniquely. The two moduli have dense ranges in their supports, and their intertwining by the polar map yields both formulas for the adjoint on its natural domain.

clause: Polar blocks on active supports and zero extensions
evidence_or_owed: Section 3 defines R and I as bounded blocks in V and V*, then uses their zero extensions on the full carrier.

clause: Active Hilbert and Krein adjoints, squares, preservation, zero extensions and I=JR
evidence_or_owed: The graph and control discussions give both adjoint types, active square signs and the zero extension; the rotation calculation also uses JI=R.

clause: Full carrier support-square identities and vanishing on the harmonic space
evidence_or_owed: On the full direct sum the two bounded polar factors square to the total support projection and its negative, respectively. Both vanish on the harmonic space.

clause: Commuting polar factorizations of both weighted branches
evidence_or_owed: Each weighted odd branch factors through the square root of the Laplacian and its bounded polar phase in either order. The intertwining of the moduli gives equality of the two product domains.

clause: Generalized inverse and extension from its natural range
evidence_or_owed: Spectral calculus gives the inverse square root with value zero on the kernel and its natural domain. On the range of the square root the products recover the bounded polar phases. Density gives unique extensions to the active space and zero action gives the full-carrier phases.

clause: Support-normalized signed transitions
evidence_or_owed: Replacing the channel by its bounded polar partial isometry yields two signed triangular maps on the full direct sum.

clause: Algebra of the normalized transitions
evidence_or_owed: The normalized maps have zero squares, are mutual Krein adjoints and give the rotation and reflection by sum and difference. Their negative ordered products are the individual sector support projections. Their sum is the total support.

clause: Rotation formula, unitarity, quarter turn and pointwise fixed inactive complement
evidence_or_owed: Section 3 gives the exponential and trigonometric formula on the active carrier, the π/2 action, and the inactive action. Together these specify the full rotation.

clause: Strong continuity, group law and values at π and 2π
evidence_or_owed: The exponential of the bounded polar rotation generator is a norm-continuous unitary group. At pi it is minus the identity on the active space and the identity on its complement. At two pi it is the identity everywhere.

clause: Two-step polar sign
evidence_or_owed: The active polar complex structure has square −I and its full extension vanishes on the inactive space.

clause: Distinction from connection holonomy
draft_quote: Holonomy requires a connection and transport around an actual loop in the parameter space.
evidence_or_owed: The polar complex structure has the algebraic return sign on its active support. Connection holonomy requires parallel transport around a closed parameter-space path.

clause: Ordinary and reduced groups and the closed-range case
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 defines both quotients and identifies when the range closures can be omitted.

clause: Non-Hausdorff ordinary quotient and Hilbert reduced quotient
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 gives the nonclosed-range example and represents the reduced quotient isometrically by the orthogonal defect.

clause: Sectorwise and total orthogonal decompositions, including the closed-range simplification
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 states the full three-term split, obtains the two sector splits by orthogonal complements, and justifies removal of both closures.

clause: Orthogonal representatives and reduced total cohomology; ordinary case for closed range
evidence_or_owed: The proposition computes the quotient norm and projection to ker A*, identifies the harmonic sum, and treats the closed-range case.

clause: Operator/domain equivalence and bounded Borel calculus on supports
evidence_or_owed: The proposition and proof give conjugacy by V including domains and its consequence for bounded Borel functions.

clause: Nonzero spectral projections and multiplicities
evidence_or_owed: The proof pairs all positive-spectrum Borel projections, including continuous spectrum, and supplies inverse isometries on the corresponding eigenspaces.

clause: Positive-energy normalized forward and backward eigenvector maps
evidence_or_owed: Both formulas and the inverse-isometry statement occur in the proof; they preserve norms and dimensions.

clause: Four equivalent criteria for a gap above zero on the supports
evidence_or_owed: Immediately after the proof, §7 proves closed range equivalent to the norm lower bound and states both squared form inequalities.

clause: Gap of the full active Laplacian
evidence_or_owed: The two sector lower bounds combine to give the same squared lower bound for the Laplacian on its active support, with the harmonic space removed.

clause: Closed range, finite kernel and defect, and their difference
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 lists all three Fredholm conditions and defines the index with input degree zero.

clause: Euler characteristic and graded harmonic trace
evidence_or_owed: The graded trace of the harmonic projection gives the difference of ordinary cohomology dimensions under closed range.

clause: Closed range, common finite kernel, zero ungraded index and graded balance
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 gives the precise domain, range and kernels of the two odd combinations under Fredholmness and computes the ungraded and graded indices.

clause: Trace formula for the heat operator
evidence_or_owed: The equation gives the difference of its two sector traces as Tr(J exp(−tΔ)).

clause: Definition for any block-diagonal trace-class operator
evidence_or_owed: The graded trace of a block-diagonal trace-class operator is the input-sector trace minus the output-sector trace. The heat expression is its specialization.

clause: Trace-class heat supertrace identity
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 proves the constant index for each t>0 at which both sector heat operators are trace class, covering the source hypothesis for all t.

clause: Cancellation distinguishes the harmonic imbalance from a sector heat trace
evidence_or_owed: Section 7 cancels the active parts and explains why the shift with an infinite ordinary heat trace does not admit this trace calculation.

clause: Tangent operators of a moving subspace are odd and fall under the single-map results
draft_quote: A moving subspace adds no new algebra at one point and in one direction.
evidence_or_owed: The opening claim of TAUM's section. Anticommutation with the moving symmetry is part of the proposition.

clause: Norm-C2 field of orthogonal projections, locally constant dimensions and the bundle of ranges
evidence_or_owed: The direct rotation of two nearby projections proves local constancy of both dimensions and gives a local trivialization of the bundle of ranges.

clause: Symmetry and splitting induced at each point, with a fixed splitting as the constant case
evidence_or_owed: Defined, with the remark that the Hilbert inner product is fixed while the indefinite form varies with the point.

clause: Self-adjoint derivative and its two zero diagonal blocks
evidence_or_owed: Stated for a vector field of class C1 and proved by differentiating the projection identity. The decomposition into the two off-diagonal blocks is the first block form.

clause: The channel of a specified tangent direction
evidence_or_owed: The tangent map, its adjoint and the coordinate abbreviation are defined. The text adds that the map depends only on the value of the vector field at the point.

clause: Two block forms and their oriented decompositions
evidence_or_owed: The moving splitting gives both block forms. TAUM defines its oriented maps as −d and d*, so its difference and sum are exactly the displayed d + d* and d* − d.

clause: Grassmannian tangent and its Krein branch
draft_quote: It is the tangent vector to the family of subspaces.
evidence_or_owed: The derivative is identified as the Hilbert-self-adjoint tangent, and its product with the moving symmetry as Hilbert-skew-adjoint and self-adjoint for the form of that point.

clause: Projected connection on the range bundle
evidence_or_owed: Defined for sections of the moving subspaces, with its compatibility with the inner product.

clause: Commutator, compression and curvature as a mixed return
evidence_or_owed: Proved for vector fields of class C1, including the bracket term, and specialized to commuting coordinate fields as in TAUM.

clause: Ordered mixed product of two tangent channels
draft_quote: Call it the \emph{mixed return} of the two directions.
evidence_or_owed: Defined as the product of the adjoint of one tangent map with the other, on the selected subspace. In the notation of Section 7 it is d_Y* d_Z, which equals TAUM's signed product of the oriented pair.

clause: Antisymmetrization of oriented excursions
evidence_or_owed: The curvature is displayed as the difference of the two mixed returns, with their order, in the differential notation of Section 7.

clause: Positivity of a single return
draft_quote: The returns $A^*A$ and $AA^*$ are positive self-adjoint operators.
evidence_or_owed: The graded Laplacian paragraph identifies A*A as a positive self-adjoint return.

clause: Directional mixed returns and nonzero curvature
draft_quote: Curvature is thus not the return of one map.
evidence_or_owed: The contrast between one positive return and the antisymmetric exchange of two directions is stated, with the consequence that a one-parameter family has no curvature. The worked example shows two tangent maps into the same complex line whose imaginary ratio makes the mixed return anti-Hermitian.

clause: Frame connection, adjoint sign and curvature matrix
evidence_or_owed: Frames, the connection matrix and its curvature are defined. Part (a) of the proposition gives the anti-Hermitian sign. Local existence of frames is shown by a formula.

clause: Fiber compression and change of orthonormal frame
evidence_or_owed: Parts (b) and (c). The proof uses the action of the connection on coefficient vectors in place of TAUM's differential-form identity.

clause: Loop transport in a local frame
evidence_or_owed: The transport equation in a frame and the unitary matrix of a loop are given. Transport is also defined without a frame, for subspaces of any dimension and loops that leave a frame domain.

clause: Cycle sign on the active support
evidence_or_owed: The complex structure squares to minus the identity on the active carrier.

clause: Distinction from geometric holonomy
draft_quote: Holonomy in this sense should be kept apart from the sign
evidence_or_owed: The algebraic square of the polar rotation is distinguished from transport around a loop.

clause: Fiberwise fixed-channel identities for tangent channels
evidence_or_owed: Both squares are proved. The paragraph after the proposition states that each tangent map is an instance of the single-map structure of Sections 2, 3 and 7 and that the new content is the relation between directions.

clause: Summary: the symmetry turns the tangent into the form-self-adjoint operator, and curvature is the antisymmetrized mixed return
evidence_or_owed: Both halves of TAUM's boxed summary are displayed equations.

clause: Curvature two-form of a smooth finite-rank field and its components
evidence_or_owed: Defined with the convention that relates the two-form to its coordinate components.

clause: Closed form, invariant class and first Chern form
evidence_or_owed: Closedness is proved directly from the oddness of the derivative. Independence of the connection and the identification with the Chern character are cited to the Chern-Weil theorem and not reproved. The first Chern form and its components are displayed.

clause: Higher-degree Chern character
evidence_or_owed: Displayed for every degree with its factorial and normalization, and shown to equal the trace of the projection times a power of its derivative.

clause: Integral first Chern flux
evidence_or_owed: Proved for every finite rank by a triangulation and the determinants of edge transports. TAUM's statement is the case of rank one. The sentence after the proof covers smooth singular cycles. The identification of the integer with the Chern pairing is cited.

clause: Hermitian convention for the flux
draft_quote: The convention here is anti-Hermitian.
evidence_or_owed: The corollary is restated for the Hermitian two-form.

clause: Holonomy and characteristic number
draft_quote: The holonomy of a loop is not quantized.
evidence_or_owed: The determinant of the holonomy of a loop bounding a disc is the exponential of minus the flux of the trace through it, which need not be trivial for a contractible loop. The integer belongs to a closed surface. The paragraph also separates curvature at a point from holonomy of a loop.

clause: Second Chern character and interpretation of characteristic numbers
draft_quote: Identifying a characteristic number with a physical charge requires additional data
evidence_or_owed: The degree-four form is displayed. The caution about physical charge is carried.

clause: Hilbert block coupling
evidence_or_owed: Section 8 assumes self-adjoint diagonal compressions and bounded C from the prepared space to its complement together with the adjoint coupling.

clause: Common signed generator and domain
evidence_or_owed: The same bounded coupling joins two self-adjoint diagonal operators. Both signs have the direct sum of the two diagonal domains as their operator domain.

clause: Hilbert adjoint of the positive branch
evidence_or_owed: The positive branch adds the bounded self-adjoint odd operator to the self-adjoint diagonal generator, giving a self-adjoint operator on the diagonal domain.

clause: Decomposition into odd branches and Krein adjoint
evidence_or_owed: The two couplings are the Hilbert and Krein odd branches of the same channel. The grading preserves the diagonal domain and conjugates the Hilbert adjoint of the negative branch back to that branch.

clause: Hilbert Schur pencil
evidence_or_owed: The operator inside the inverse is the prepared-space Hilbert block minus z and minus the complementary resolvent return.

clause: Signed effective operator and pencil
evidence_or_owed: For each sign the effective operator subtracts the signed self-energy from the retained diagonal operator. Subtracting the spectral parameter gives the closed pencil on that diagonal domain.

clause: Hilbert corner on the common resolvent set
evidence_or_owed: Section 8 solves the complementary block equation to obtain the compressed resolvent for a Hilbert decomposition and bounded coupling. The physical pair uses this inside its output space.

clause: Full triangular factorization and invertibility equivalence
evidence_or_owed: At a resolvent point of the complementary block, triangular factors reduce the shifted full operator to the pencil and the shifted complementary block. The full resolvent exists exactly when the pencil is boundedly invertible.

clause: Full inverse and Krein corner
evidence_or_owed: The inverse has all four signed blocks in their composition order. The retained-sector corner is the inverse pencil for either sign, including the Krein coupling.

clause: Hilbert return through the complementary resolvent
evidence_or_owed: The return is C*(H_Q-z)⁻¹C and the text specifies the exit, propagation and re-entry through the complementary subspace.

clause: Return in the signed orientation algebra
evidence_or_owed: The signed forward orientation, complementary resolvent extended by zero, and backward orientation compose to minus the self-energy on the retained sector. This gives the oriented formula for the effective operator.

clause: Subtraction on the positive branch
evidence_or_owed: The Hilbert corner has a subtracted self-energy.

clause: Addition on the Krein branch and source of the relative sign
evidence_or_owed: The lower coupling changes sign between the two adjoint classes. Eliminating the complement therefore adds the same resolvent return to the retained generator in the Krein branch.

clause: Analyticity and adjoint symmetry
evidence_or_owed: The bounded compression of the self-adjoint complementary resolvent is norm analytic on its resolvent set and takes conjugate arguments to Hilbert adjoints.

clause: Positive imaginary part for complex energy
evidence_or_owed: In the upper half-plane the imaginary part of the self-energy factors through the complementary resolvent as a positive operator. Its quadratic form is the imaginary part of the spectral parameter times a squared norm.

clause: Hilbert effective operator in the upper half-plane
evidence_or_owed: The imaginary part of the Hilbert effective operator on its domain is minus the positive imaginary part of the self-energy in the upper half-plane.

clause: Opposite sign for the Krein effective operator
evidence_or_owed: The imaginary part of the Krein effective operator on its domain is the positive imaginary part of that same self-energy in the upper half-plane.

clause: Positive return and lowered effective form below the complementary spectrum
evidence_or_owed: The text after the elimination proof gives a positive semidefinite self-energy at real energies below the complementary spectrum, and the displayed Hilbert formula subtracts it.

clause: Strict positivity of the complementary resolvent
evidence_or_owed: Below the bottom of the complementary spectrum, integration against its spectral measure gives strictly positive resolvent expectation on each nonzero vector. The return is positive semidefinite on the retained sector.

clause: Raised effective form of the opposite branch
evidence_or_owed: At a real parameter below the complementary spectrum the Krein effective form adds the same nonnegative return that the Hilbert effective form subtracts.

clause: Resolvent-dressed return
evidence_or_owed: The exit, complementary resolvent, and adjoint return occur explicitly in the measured Hilbert pencil.

clause: Antisymmetrized tangent return and its common typing with self-energy
evidence_or_owed: The tangent return passes through the identity on the complement, and its antisymmetrization gives the curvature. The Schur self-energy passes through the complementary resolvent. Both return to the retained space.

clause: Hilbert-self-adjoint generator, bounded port, nonreal resolvent
draft_quote: Throughout this section $\mathcal X$ is a complex Hilbert space
evidence_or_owed: The opening fixes a self-adjoint H in a Hilbert space, a bounded port from a port space of any dimension, and the nonreal resolvent. Section 1 states the same hypotheses on the output space.

clause: Compressed resolvent of a bounded port
evidence_or_owed: The displayed equation defines the response on the complement of the real axis for a port space of any dimension.

clause: Scope of the definition: interior, finite-rank and regularized singular inputs (following discussion)
draft_quote: It covers a port inside the system, a port of finite rank, and a singular input
evidence_or_owed: TAUM's sentence after the definition is carried in the opening.

clause: Holomorphy off the real axis and adjoint symmetry
evidence_or_owed: Stated and proved from norm analyticity and the adjoint symmetry of the resolvent.

clause: Positive imaginary part and its exact factorization on the upper half-plane
evidence_or_owed: The proof compresses the one-point resolvent identity and exhibits the imaginary part as a positive operator.

clause: Two-point Nevanlinna kernel
evidence_or_owed: Defined on pairs of points of the upper half-plane.

clause: Two-point resolvent factorization and positive kernel
evidence_or_owed: The two-point resolvent identity gives the factorization. The quadratic sum is displayed as a squared norm for every finite choice of points and port vectors.

clause: Positive self-adjoint return on the input sector
evidence_or_owed: Part (a) uses the positive self-adjoint return stated after the cohomology formula of Section 7.

clause: Canonical compressed resolvent for the A*A choice
evidence_or_owed: The canonical response is displayed for every bounded input into the physical space.

clause: Herglotz and positive-kernel conclusions for this choice
evidence_or_owed: Part (a) applies both propositions with H equal to the return.

clause: Port identity on the retained sector
evidence_or_owed: Part (b) compresses the Schur formula of Section 8 by a port that maps into the retained space.

clause: Passive response of the full Hilbert block
evidence_or_owed: The block operator is self-adjoint as a bounded symmetric perturbation of the direct sum of its diagonal blocks, so its response through the embedded port satisfies both propositions.

clause: Limit of positivity for the Krein branch
draft_quote: No such positivity is assumed here.
evidence_or_owed: Established by a witness: a two-by-two generator self-adjoint for the indefinite form, with real eigenvalues 1 and 2, whose response through the first coordinate has imaginary part -6/5 at z = 2 + i/2. Which further assumptions restore positivity is a separate question and is not part of this clause.

clause: Operator Cayley transform of the passive response
evidence_or_owed: Defined on the upper half-plane.

clause: Bounded invertibility of the Cayley denominator
evidence_or_owed: First statement of the proposition, with the lower bounds for the operator and its adjoint, closed dense range, and an inverse of norm at most one for port spaces of any dimension.

clause: Analyticity, defect identity and contractivity
evidence_or_owed: The congruence with four times the imaginary part is derived and the norm bound follows.

clause: Operator-valued de Branges–Rovnyak kernel
evidence_or_owed: Defined with the denominator and sign convention of TAUM.

clause: Kernel factorization, positivity and reproducing space
evidence_or_owed: The factorization with the two Cayley factors and the factor two is proved, and positivity follows by congruence. The reproducing-kernel consequence is stated with a citation and is not reproved.

clause: Positive operator weights at the response lines
evidence_or_owed: The paragraph after the definition identifies the atoms of the measure with the weights of Corollary 1.3.

clause: Borel measure and total mass for arbitrary spectra
evidence_or_owed: Defined on all Borel sets with total mass, weak countable additivity, and the scalar complex measures used for integration.

clause: Finite-line resolvent and Fourier sums
evidence_or_owed: Both finite sums are displayed after the proposition, for weights of any rank.

clause: General resolvent and time-domain representations
evidence_or_owed: Both operator-valued integrals are stated for an arbitrary compressed spectral measure, with the factor of Planck's constant used in the draft.

clause: Time-domain positive definiteness
evidence_or_owed: The quadratic sum is displayed as the squared norm of a sum of evolved port vectors.

clause: Closed span generated from the port in time
evidence_or_owed: Section 1 defines the space by the time span. The proposition restates it for a port.

clause: Nonreal resolvent-span definition, equivalence, and minimality terminology
draft_quote: is called \emph{minimal} when
evidence_or_owed: The proposition proves that the resolvent span and the time span coincide for arbitrary spectra, by the Laplace representation of the resolvent in one direction and invariance under all resolvents in the other. The sentence after it defines a minimal pair.

clause: Contains the direct range and is invariant under the entire unitary group
evidence_or_owed: Stated in the proposition and proved from the strong limit of the scaled resolvent.

clause: Reducing self-adjoint restriction and exact response invariance
evidence_or_owed: The restriction is self-adjoint, the two responses agree at every nonreal point, and the restricted pair is minimal.

clause: Unique unitary intertwining generators and ports for equal responses
evidence_or_owed: Full proof: equal Gram matrices of resolvent-port vectors, extension by minimality, intertwining of resolvents and hence of generators with their domains, recovery of the ports, and uniqueness. Two continuity steps are written out: the conjugate pair of points in the Gram formula, which TAUM mentions, and equal points in the resolvent identity, which it does not.

clause: Rank count for the indirect space and decomposition of the full defect
evidence_or_owed: Section 1 proves the count and the adjoint-kernel decomposition. The discussion of weight ranges restates the finite-rank hypothesis.

clause: Port-coordinate invariance and the rank condition for injectivity (following discussion)
draft_quote: an invertible change of coordinates $T$ on $\mathcal E$ preserves it
evidence_or_owed: The first remark gives invariance under a change of port coordinates. The last sentences give the kernel condition for an injective port.

clause: Relations between the weight ranges (following discussion)
draft_quote: The count is the dimension of the space of relations
